# The honest shape of the topology verify_truncate_orphan_merge_workflow.txt
# attacks: a repository whose mainline never had a vault merges one in from a
# branch. The log's history hangs off the merge's second parent, so the walk
# crosses over there - and has to find nothing wrong, all the way down to the
# trust anchor.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

# A mainline without any vault.
cp note note.txt
exec git add note.txt
exec git commit -m 'no vault here'

# The vault is born on a branch and grows there.
exec git switch -c vault
exec sesam init --user admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'sesam init'
exec sesam add s.txt --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secret'

# Back on the mainline, merged in with a real merge commit.
exec git switch -
# sesam's pre-merge-commit hook hands the finalize back to `git commit`, which
# is the flow it tells the user to follow.
! exec git merge --no-ff --no-edit vault
exec git commit --no-edit

exec git rev-list --first-parent HEAD
stdout -count=2 '^[0-9a-f]{40}$'

exec sesam verify --truncate
stderr 'Audit log history: ok'

-- s.txt --
top secret
-- note --
unrelated file
